unit_result_entry.title: Prime-log independence identifies torus distributions with vertical asymptotic distributions
unit_result_entry.why_material: Linear independence of log primes makes long vertical averages of continuous functions equal Haar averages on the finite torus; hence the torus measures are exactly the asymptotic value and derivative-weighted distributions of partial Euler products, and their densities give second derivatives of finite-product Jensen functions.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This is the deterministic bridge from abstract phase variables back to actual vertical motion.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: High for Fourier-transform formulas and constants; equidistribution and its consequence are prose-clear.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Exponentiation transports log-value distributions to zeta-value distributions
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The exponential map sends log-value measures to value measures and transforms densities by summing over all logarithms with the Jacobian factor; Gaussian decay makes these periodized sums and all derivatives converge, giving smoothness, positivity away from zero, analyticity after composition, and boundary-weighted vanishing.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Log-zeta value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 13 identifies the asymptotic distribution of log zeta, expresses the Jensen function of log zeta minus x as a logarithmic potential, proves twice differentiability with curvature 2π times the weighted density, and derives exact mean motions and strip zero frequencies by integrating that density; it also records boundary divergence and the conjugate negative-height version.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Partial Euler products first supply ordinary almost-periodic objects whose torus laws are exact by equidistribution, then generalized convergence theorems transfer their Jensen functions and distributions to zeta and log zeta.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated mean convergence and branch-domain hypotheses and does not extend automatically beyond Re(s)>1/2.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Zeta-value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 14 gives the parallel statements for zeta minus x: asymptotic distribution, logarithmic-potential Jensen formula, curvature from the weighted zeta-value density, mean motions, and density-integral zero frequencies; its proof uses the exponential pushforward and relates zeta Jensen functions to all logarithmic preimages.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Zeta-value densities are periodized, Jacobian-adjusted pushforwards of log-zeta densities, allowing regularity and curvature results to transfer while creating a distinguished behavior at value zero and multiple logarithmic preimages.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Boundary statements need the explicit |x|-weights recorded in Theorem 12; unweighted uniform vanishing is false.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Exponentiation preserves the distribution program but changes singular behavior

related_synthesis_entries.claim: As the log-Euler variance diverges at Re(s)=1/2, pointwise density flattens while the logarithmic-potential/Jensen quantities grow, producing increasing zero frequencies across the full half-plane.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source establishes asymptotic distribution and zero-frequency consequences in Re(s)>1/2, not any assertion about the location of zeta zeros on the critical line.
